about.title: About Me
about.bio1: I'm a Backend Developer at Port Louis, working on a serverless audit automation ecosystem. I develop and maintain crawlers that interact with court portals, boards of trade, public agencies, and municipal services to issue certificates, track requests, and capture payment slips and case records.
about.bio2: I work across the full technical lifecycle with JSON workflows executed by Puppeteer, REST integrations, CAPTCHA, and proxies. The pipeline includes downloading and persisting artifacts in Amazon S3, document identification, and TypeScript readers that extract and validate PDF data through regex, OCR, and business rules.
about.bio3: I also troubleshoot production issues by correlating rendered DOM state, logs, payloads, and relationships among audits, certificates, entities, and tasks. I validate fixes with Jest, focused staging runs, and persisted-file evidence, applying the QA discipline I developed while working on SGDoctor.
about.goalDescription: Backend development applied to integrations, document automation, and process reliability.
about.differentialDescription: Combined experience in development, testing, requirements analysis, and production troubleshooting.

education.title: Academic Education
education.institution: State University of Southwest Bahia - UESB

responsibilities: Developed and enhanced more than 15 automation workflows for issuing, capturing, and reading certificates, payment slips, and public records, including integrations with TURS, TRF1, TRF5, MPT, MPMT, TCU, CETESB, SEMAE, and SAESA SCS, among others.

Implemented JSON-parameterized crawlers and TypeScript readers using Puppeteer, REST APIs, regex, CAPTCHA solving, PDF manipulation, modal and outage handling, task rescheduling, and integrated tests in local and staging environments through AWS Lambda.

Delivered more than 40 production improvements during the first few months, spanning more than 20 project components. The optimizations reduced execution time by up to 23% in specific workflows and decreased failures and manual interventions by 20% to 30% across the supported automations.

items.company: CPDS - Centro de Pesquisa e Desenvolvimento de Software
responsibilities: Developed the back end of a clinical and academic platform, structuring the complete patient-care workflow, including scheduling, patient records, clinical notes, procedures, documents, validation, and digital signatures with history and traceability.

Implemented the workflows using Laravel, PHP, Eloquent, and PostgreSQL, applying Controller-Service-Repository architecture, migrations, relationships between clinical entities, role-based permission middleware, transactions with lockForUpdate, concurrency handling, notifications, and integration across care, user, and inventory modules.

This reduced user provisioning time by 70% to 90%, cut rework during medical-record validation by 30% to 50%, and blocked 100% of inventory movements above the available balance covered by the system rules, while ensuring full traceability of signatures and clinical changes.
